obligations.title: Otherwise identical streams differing in one Resource, Scope, metric property or point attribute remain distinct
obligations.note: Demonstrated: otherwise identical streams differing in one supported compatibility dimension - the compatibility Resource service.* tuple, a promoted Scope label, a metric property or a point attribute - stay distinct through the native and ordinary receiver routes. Decision 1 is decided (2026-11-15) and is retained here as provenance, not implementation evidence. Not demonstrated: Entity-aware Resource identity, typed Entity IDs, absent-versus-empty fallback presence and malformed/duplicate EntityRef rejection (gap-entity-identity, whose target cases are recorded in resource_identity_fallback), and complete Scope-injective stream identity, which decision 1 explicitly defers as a current-phase limitation.

obligations.title: Forced series/content candidate-hash collisions are rejected or disambiguated by complete labels/content and never merged
obligations.note: Complete-label collision guards exist (sharedSeriesLabels and associateWithHistory return ErrSeriesHashCollision), but a 64-bit labels.StableHash collision cannot be constructed from a test without a production injection point. Decision 1 now states that hashes are lookup and candidate encodings, never substitutes for complete canonical identity and complete-content comparison; the target case identity-candidate-collision in resource_identity_fallback records the accepted rule. No production hook was added and no forced-collision coverage is claimed.

obligations.title: One descriptive Resource change shared by 10,000 member series creates one owner version and no membership changes
obligations.note: The members_10000 subtest asserts one version for the change, an unchanged membership start for every member, and the pre/post content band.

obligations.title: A/B/A at successive effective times returns exactly those bands, and backfilled observations do not move validity successors
obligations.note: The fixture association_history_and_replay probes info() immediately before and at each boundary. It asserts A/B/A as three epochs, that a backfilled observation extends only the epoch it observes, that a late actual B change starts at its effective time and ends the predecessor A epoch exclusively, and that a backfilled B equal to its immediate successor coalesces that successor while preserving both observation histories. The unit tests remain the direct boundary checks.

obligations.title: A matching content version and membership overlapping disjoint parts of a query range return no series
obligations.note: The scrape-owner case has a series whose job-a membership is [2500,2800) and whose matching 15s versions are [1000,2000) and [3000,inf). The query [1000,3000] overlaps each of them but not jointly, so the series is absent, while its sibling memberships are reported.

obligations.title: A valid metadata prefix followed by a conflict publishes no samples, metadata, index prefix, WAL prefix or committed counters
obligations.note: The fixture rollback_conflict batches a valid new association, a conflicting owner content version and a sample, then repeats with a same-time competing membership on a series that is already associated, and asserts the error class, the unchanged complete state, unchanged committed-work counters and an unchanged WAL segment count in both cases. The observation tests cover the same rejection without a fixture.

obligations.title: Owner-only and observation-bound publication produces exact metadata, no fabricated samples and zero sample-payload reads
obligations.note: The fixture publishes an unchanged observation and a changed one against a block-backed store, asserts the exact owner history, committed-work counters, that no sample series or sample time coverage appears, and that the metadata-only read opens no sample payload.

obligations.title: WAL replay, flush/reopen, compaction/reopen, retention and metadata-only replay retain exactly the specified state or an explicit truncation state
obligations.note: The float fixture compares the same query before flush, after flush and after reopen on the columnar route and on stock TSDB. Retention truncation is asserted as an explicit Truncated bit, not as expired validity. association_history_and_replay asserts that ordered content and membership histories survive WAL replay, and association_replay_and_truncation asserts that a bounded retained history and its explicit truncation survive replay without manufacturing versions or bounds.

obligations.title: Enrichment uses the applicable band, preserves unassociated series, honours explicit filters and never duplicates a series through ownership transitions
obligations.note: Both fixtures assert complete vector results at each boundary, that an unassociated series survives an unfiltered aggregation, and that a filtered aggregation selects only matching series without multiplying an input.

obligations.title: Filtered candidates, intermediate cursors, exact-full/final/empty pages, latest/projection views and sibling pagers produce complete expected sequences without repeats or omissions
obligations.note: The selected isolation contract is the current positional owner/row cursor, and only that contract is asserted. Snapshot isolation across pages is decision 7 and is recorded as blocked rather than assumed.

obligations.title: Equivalent OTLP and OTAP inputs produce the same target-native state and a separately specified legacy view; resets, retries, unsupported input and negative acknowledgements create no phantom identity or exactly-once claim
obligations.note: Equivalence covers stored samples and metric metadata; the legacy target_info projection is asserted separately by the ordinary-route tests. A transport acknowledgement is explicitly not an exactly-once claim, and no retry-duplication test asserts otherwise.

obligations.title: Kubernetes node totals, rollout totals, unattributed series, same-name/different-UID objects and rejected contradictory associations equal the hand-authored results
obligations.note: Demonstrated: node A filtered 100+200 MiB = 300 MiB and unfiltered 350 MiB with the unattributed 50 MiB series retained; old 0.2 + new 0.3 cores = 0.5 with every input counted once; same-name series kept apart by explicit identifying attributes. Decision 2 is decided: a contradictory association at the same series/kind/effective time is rejected atomically rather than retained unresolved, evidenced by gap-conflict-resolution and rollback_conflict. Not demonstrated: collection-time acquisition through a plain scrape (decision 4, gap-k8s-acquisition) and identifying same-name/different-UID objects without an explicit distinguishing attribute (decision 1, gap-entity-identity).

obligations.title: Floats including signed zero and NaN bit patterns, integer and float native histograms, start timestamps, staleness and exemplars survive each supported route and lifecycle operation
obligations.note: Demonstrated: exact float and native histogram payloads, per-sample start timestamps on the columnar route and on explicitly ST-enabled stock TSDB, and staleness markers on the routes that carry them. Not demonstrated: exemplar survival on the scalar and scrape routes (the appender accepts an exemplar and stores nothing - gap-exemplars, a recorded defect), and native histograms, summaries or exemplars through the native OTAP sink, which rejects them explicitly before storage (gap-otap-native-samples).

obligations.title: Resource, Scope, metric properties and point attributes survive until authoritative stream resolution
obligations.note: Demonstrated: Resource, Scope, metric-property and point-attribute context survives to the supported compatibility identity (the reserved service.* label tuple) and to per-series Metric, Resource and Scope owners. Decision 1 is decided and retained as provenance. Not demonstrated: complete Entity-aware Resource identity, typed Entity IDs and the absent-versus-empty fallback, which are gap-entity-identity (target cases in resource_identity_fallback).

obligations.title: Complete labels and complete typed content are authoritative after candidate lookup
obligations.note: Demonstrated: complete labels and the complete string content are authoritative after candidate lookup; a hash only locates a candidate and every semantic decision re-checks the real content. Not demonstrated: complete typed content, because only strings are representable (gap-typed-content).

obligations.title: OTAP batch/table IDs, dictionaries, temporal batches and acknowledgements are not durable identities and provide no exactly-once delivery
obligations.note: Dictionary and reference deltas are exercised; no test claims exactly-once delivery. association_replay_and_truncation repeats an ordinary storage transaction with the same sample and metadata and records the duplicate rejection rather than a deduplicated success, so no exactly-once delivery is implied and no phantom Resource identity is created. That is storage-boundary evidence; OTAP/OTLP reset and receiver-retry semantics remain outside this package.

obligations.title: Metadata domains and per-series histories remain independent rather than one family-global history
EffectiveFrom is inclusive and actual successors end predecessor validity exclusively
obligations.note: The fixture association_history_and_replay probes immediately before and at each boundary, including a backfilled B change point that ends the predecessor A epoch exclusively.

obligations.title: Observation bounds do not imply expiry or prove exact history over discarded or ambiguous observations
obligations.note: Truncation is reported as an explicit bit; observation bounds never become validity bounds. association_replay_and_truncation asserts that a discarded oldest version is reported as history_truncated and is not resurrected by a query or by replay.

obligations.title: Same-time content and membership conflicts have deterministic outcomes; map order or newest-arrival selection is forbidden
obligations.note: Decision 2 is decided: same-time differing content and same-time differing membership both reject the whole transaction atomically, with no map-order or arrival-order selection. Fixed-case-6 and invariant-8 assert the complete rollback, and rollback_conflict exercises both conflict classes. Retaining an explicitly unresolved association is no longer a target requirement.

obligations.title: Rejected transactions publish no samples, metadata, index prefix, WAL prefix or committed-work counters
Metadata-only publication creates no samples or sample time coverage
Existing queries and vector matching ignore metadata by default; deliberate promotion appears only in final label-visible output
obligations.note: Plain selectors and the built-in PromQL suite run over a store that holds metadata without any metadata label appearing.

obligations.title: Unassociated series survive enrichment, enrichment contributes each input series at most once, and contradictory associations are rejected rather than retained unresolved
obligations.note: Demonstrated: unassociated series survive enrichment and each input series contributes at most once, including across ownership transitions. Decision 2 selects atomic rejection for contradictory associations, so no stored unresolved association is implied or tested; that rejection is asserted by TestMetadataObservationConflictsLeaveNoState and rollback_conflict.

obligations.title: Reverse queries validate a common overlap of content validity, association validity and query range before reading samples
obligations.note: The disjoint-member series is absent while its neighbours are reported, and the reverse queries assert zero sample-payload opens.

obligations.title: Metadata-only and irrelevant-pruned paths open zero sample payloads
obligations.note: The fixtures assert SamplePayloadOpens and SegmentsRead are zero for metadata-only reads of a block-backed store.

obligations.title: Buffers, arrays, maps and content have documented owners, borrow/copy rules, release points and bounded cache/pool budgets at the interface definitions
obligations.note: Ownership is documented only in places (Content.Clone, BatchSeries comments); there is no bounded cache/pool budget and no lifetime test. Admission and truncation budgets are decision 9.

obligations.title: Local bounded mutable state feeds immutable parts through atomic visibility, with explicit replay and retention behaviour
obligations.note: Race-detector coverage is limited to the interleavings executed by the suite; no claim is made about untested schedules.

obligations.title: tmpfs/WAL-off measurements are not physical-disk durability or sustainable-throughput evidence
obligations.note: This is a reporting rule for any future measurement, not an executable assertion. N0 runs no timing work.

obligations.title: Prometheus does not inherit distributed transactions, replication, tenant placement or a metadata RPC to satisfy external installations' scale
obligations.note: An architecture-scope rule recorded for review; nothing in N0 adds distribution.

obligations.title: Scope identity does not distinguish otherwise identical streams in the current phase
obligations.note: Decision 1 explicitly defers Scope-injective stream identity for the current phase. Scope metadata is still retained, versioned and queryable as its own owner kind; resource_identity_fallback asserts that survival without claiming that Scope alone distinguishes otherwise identical streams. Metric properties and data-point attributes remain distinct logical stream dimensions under existing translation semantics.

obligations.title: A real scrape executes parsing, relabeling, metadata forwarding and commit into the columnar store
obligations.note: A real scrape pool, real HTTP target and real scrape loop run with the columnar store as the AppendableV2. Exact samples, a target-group label, a metric relabel drop, forwarded type/help/unit metadata, a report sample and a staleness marker after the series disappears are asserted. The separate concurrency-scalar-appenders obligation keeps the direct AppenderV2 concurrency test, which is not scrape evidence.

obligations.title: The ordinary OTLP receiver route reaches the columnar store with its legacy projection
obligations.note: The legacy target_info view is asserted separately from the native metadata state.

obligations.title: The native OTAP receiver route reaches the columnar store
obligations.note: Unsupported payloads are rejected before storage (gap-otap-native-samples).

obligations.title: The experimental metadata HTTP surface reaches the store
obligations.note: The fixtures drive /resources through httptest with the real handler, including an explicit history_truncated response. Which response fields are contractual is decision 7.

obligations.title: PromQL info() enrichment reaches the store through the engine
obligations.note: Current info() semantics only, including absent and explicitly truncated histories. PR99 grammar and promotion syntax are decision 6.

obligations.title: Remote-write requests are executed against the columnar store and stock TSDB
obligations.note: Real RW1 and RW2 requests run through remote.NewWriteHandler. Stock TSDB accepts them and preserves exact float bits, timestamps, integer and float native histograms, RW2 start timestamps, symbol-derived labels, exemplars and response statistics; duplicate, out-of-order, invalid-label and invalid-metadata-symbol requests produce the stock-compatible 400 responses with the expected written-sample headers. The columnar route rejects every RW1 and RW2 request with HTTP 500 because its appender does not implement storage.ExemplarAppenderV2, and writes nothing (gap-rw-exemplar-appender). Per-series metadata is not demonstrated on either route: RW1 request metadata is ignored by the receiver, and stock TSDB's native metadata has no exported read surface. Reopened/replayed RW state is not demonstrated either: teststorage offers no reopen helper and the columnar route stores nothing. RW1 also cannot carry a negative zero sample value (proto3 implicit presence omits -0.0), which is a protocol representation difference, not a store behaviour. The remote-write contract is therefore not covered, and complete architecture comparison remains blocked for it.

obligations.title: Identical logical samples produce identical stored state and query results on the columnar route and on stock TSDB
obligations.note: Bit-exact differential sample rendering across both routes, including float edge cases and native histograms. Route representation differences are recorded separately (route-difference-stock-start-timestamps).

obligations.title: Independent scalar AppenderV2 transactions commit and remain selectable under concurrency
obligations.note: TestConcurrentScalarAppendersShareCommittedTail drives 64 goroutines with their own AppenderV2 transactions; it is a scalar append-concurrency obligation only. It does not parse, relabel or commit a scrape, so it is not scrape-route evidence (see route-scrape).

obligations.title: Stock TSDB with default options does not retain a per-sample start timestamp
obligations.note: Stock TSDB with default options does not retain a per-sample start timestamp: default XOR chunks return AtST()==0 and the default Options leave EnableSTStorage false. That is a legacy-configuration fact, not a stock TSDB defect. tsdb.Options.EnableSTStorage exists; with EnableSTStorage=true, FloatChunkEncoding=EncXOR2 and EnableHistogramSTEncoding=true the same exact start_timestamps_across_routes fixture asserts ST=1500 before and after head compaction on route tsdb_st. N0's statement that the option was unreachable through tsdb.Options is corrected by the dated N0-R erratum.

obligations.title: Typed metadata content (booleans, integers, doubles, arrays, maps, null, unknown)
obligations.note: Content.Attributes and every HTTP value are string-only. Boolean true versus the string "true", integer 1 versus double 1, array order, map equality and null versus absent are not representable, so no fixture may assert them. The target case identity-entity-typed-content in resource_identity_fallback records the accepted typed-content clause.

obligations.title: Entity-aware Resource identity, EntityRefs and fallback presence semantics
obligations.note: Decision 1 is decided, so this is no longer semantically blocked. The incumbent still stores only the fixed service.name/service.namespace/service.instance.id compatibility identity, ignores EntityRefs, cannot distinguish an absent fallback attribute from an explicitly empty one, and has no malformed/duplicate same-type EntityRef rejection. resource_identity_fallback executes the representable compatibility cases and records the unimplemented clauses as machine-checked target cases.

obligations.title: Source provenance chain and conflicting source claims
obligations.note: A Source owner kind exists, but which transport/sender/producer a source names is decision 5.

obligations.title: Explicit unknown, clearing and expiry semantics
obligations.note: No producer/API operation clears content or ends membership beyond a successor version, and absent versus cleared is not distinguishable. Decision 3 owns the answer.

obligations.title: Contradictory same-time associations are rejected atomically
obligations.note: The historical entry asked whether a conflicting association could be retained as explicitly unresolved. Decision 2 rejected that alternative: contradictory same-time content or membership rejects the whole transaction atomically, publishes nothing and leaves committed state unchanged. The evidence exercises both conflict classes and the complete rollback; no unresolved-retention subsystem exists or is required by the target.

obligations.title: Collection-time Kubernetes association acquisition and partial-description reconciliation
obligations.note: The arithmetic is settled and asserted with explicit associations; how a plain scrape or a collector supplies them, and whether partial descriptions merge, is decision 4.

obligations.title: Native OTAP histograms, summaries and exemplars
obligations.note: The native sink converts number data points only and rejects histograms, summaries and exemplars before storage rather than dropping them silently. That explicit rejection is safe fail-closed behaviour and is distinct from the scalar accept-then-discard exemplar defect (gap-exemplars). Widening it is production work outside this package.

obligations.title: The columnar routes accept an exemplar and silently discard it
obligations.note: Reproduced: a real OpenMetrics scrape whose sample carries an exemplar stores the sample and reports success, the store exposes no exemplar query surface, and the scalar V1 AppendExemplar returns a reference and no error while retaining nothing queryable. Silent loss is not acceptable target behaviour. The native OTAP route instead rejects exemplars explicitly before storage (gap-otap-native-samples), which is safe fail-closed behaviour and is recorded separately. No exemplar persistence is implemented here.

obligations.title: Validity-band info() execution
obligations.note: info() resolves metadata per evaluation instant rather than once per stable band. The observable results at each boundary are correct and asserted, including by association_history_and_replay; this entry records the mechanism gap without claiming a performance result.

obligations.title: Snapshot-isolated metadata pagination
obligations.note: The current cursor is a positional owner/row key, not a snapshot or retained iterator. Decision 7 owns the snapshot contract.

obligations.title: Contractual typed JSON values in metadata HTTP responses
obligations.note: Every value is a JSON string and the experimental envelope is not contractual. Decision 7 owns it.

obligations.title: target_info, promoted-label and reserved-identity-label coexistence and migration
obligations.note: The ordinary route still emits target_info and the native route uses a reserved identity label; the coexistence period and legacy API obligations are decision 8.

obligations.title: Admission, coalescing and truncation budgets under identity/content/version/membership churn
obligations.note: A per-owner version cap exists and truncation is reported, but it is not a memory bound and no admission policy is decided.

obligations.title: PR99 metadata filter/grouping/alias grammar
obligations.note: Current info() is the only implemented enrichment form. The proposal was last checked open and non-draft with 'Implementation Status: Not implemented'.

obligations.title: Representative local scales, churn, durability settings and absolute gates
obligations.note: N0 contains no corpus capture, benchmark or adoption claim; synthetic fixtures are mechanism controls only.

obligations.title: The columnar appender rejects internally inconsistent native histograms exactly like stock TSDB
obligations.note: The N0 divergence is closed. The columnar appender now validates integer and float native histograms with the model's Histogram.Validate/FloatHistogram.Validate before staging anything, at the same point as stock TSDB. A real OTLP request with a count/bucket disagreement proves the route: stock and columnar both reject it, roll back and publish nothing, while valid histograms and the model's accepted zero-count boundaries still ingest. The entry is retained as a passing obligation rather than deleted so the closed defect stays traceable.

obligations.title: The columnar appender does not implement storage.ExemplarAppenderV2, so remote write fails closed
obligations.note: storage/remote type-asserts the appender to storage.ExemplarAppenderV2 before appending anything and answers HTTP 500 when the assertion fails. The columnar *appender implements neither AppendExemplars nor exemplar persistence, so a real RW1 or RW2 request is rejected with the exact interface error and stores no sample. That is fail-closed behaviour, not silent loss; implementing the interface is production work and was not done here.
